correctness.rationale: Two complete, independent exhaustive enumerations agree exactly: every valid binary prefix through length 96 with square-suffix dynamic programming, and every nine-square product using all 154 possible overlap-free square blocks up to length 80. The latter factor bound is rigorously forced by eight remaining nonempty squares. The complete output has 12 words distributed 2,2,4,2,2 at lengths 48,76,86,92,96, each with one recipe. Both programs reproduce an embedded 12-row exact census and assert intermediate state counts. The proof is finite, not an extrapolation; larger lengths are not claimed.

value.rationale: The sharp nine-block extremal problem is the natural object of the 2026 theorem. Applying the square-preserving Thue-Morse morphism doubles a known minimal 48-symbol witness to length 96, singling out this first closed morphic scale without an arbitrary cutoff. The exact spectrum contains only five feasible total lengths (48,76,86,92,96), twelve words and six complement pairs, with strict gaps including 28 symbols between the two smallest attainable lengths. The exclusions and intermediate examples reveal nontrivial rigidity of extremal square products not implied by either the block-count obstruction or a shortest witness. This is a complete natural finite support-and-fiber classification; no all-length claim is needed for the finite result to be useful.
